drg.description: Kidney and Urinary Tract Infections without MCC

notes.text:
HISTORY AND PHYSICAL. Chart, labs and overnight events reviewed. 85-year-old male admitted for urinary tract infection. Admission data:
Day 0: labs bilirubin 0.55, creatinine 1.01, hemoglobin 14.2, platelets 203, sodium 139, wbc 8.9; vitals dbp 66-71, heart_rate 84-88, map 83-87, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 14-15, sbp 117-123, spo2 97-98, temp 36.9-37.1
Day 0 orders/meds/results: Urinalysis: positive nitrites, >50 WBC/hpf; Ceftriaxone 1 g IV
Assessment and plan: Urinary tract infection. Type 2 diabetes. Hypertension.

PROGRESS NOTE, hospital day 1. Patient seen and examined at bedside. Data:
Day 1: labs creatinine 0.98, hemoglobin 14, platelets 196, sodium 139, wbc 8.8; vitals dbp 66-71, heart_rate 85-89, map 84-88, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 14-15, sbp 118-124, spo2 97-99, temp 36.9-37.2
Day 1 orders/meds/results: Ceftriaxone 1 g IV
Assessment and plan: Urinary tract infection. Type 2 diabetes. Hypertension. Continue current management.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY. 85-year-old male, length of stay 3 days. Hospital course: treated per the plan above with daily labs and vital signs; stable for discharge. Medications reconciled and return precautions reviewed. Discharge diagnoses: Urinary tract infection. Type 2 diabetes. Hypertension. Follow up with primary care in one week. Patient seen and examined at bedside.
